questions.q: If $6$ workers can paint a fence in $10$ hours, how many hours would it take $15$ workers working at the same rate?
questions.answer: This is an inverse proportion: $\text{Workers} \times \text{Time} = \text{Constant}$. Total worker-hours $= 6 \times 10 = 60$. For $15$ workers: $\text{Time} = \frac{60}{15} = 4$ hours.

questions.q: A car travels $240\text{ km}$ using $20$ liters of fuel. How many liters are required to travel $360\text{ km}$ at the same rate?
questions.answer: Direct proportion: $\frac{240}{20} = 12\text{ km/L}$. For $360\text{ km}$: $\text{Fuel} = \frac{360}{12} = 30$ liters.

questions.q: If $a : b = 2 : 3$ and $b : c = 4 : 5$, what is the ratio $a : c$?
questions.answer: Equate $b$ by multiplying: $a : b = 8 : 12$ and $b : c = 12 : 15$. Thus, $a : c = 8 : 15$.

questions.q: A jacket originally priced at $150$ SAR is discounted by $20\%$. What is the sale price?
The price of an item was increased by $20\%$ and then decreased by $20\%$. What is the net percentage change in price?
questions.answer: Net multiplier $= (1 + 0.20)(1 - 0.20) = 1.20 \times 0.80 = 0.96$. A final factor of $0.96$ represents a $4\%$ net decrease.

questions.q: If $25\%$ of a number $x$ is $45$, what is $60\%$ of $x$?
A car travels from City A to City B at $60\text{ km/h}$ and returns along the same route at $40\text{ km/h}$. What is the average speed for the round trip?
questions.answer: Harmonic mean formula for equal distances: $v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{2 v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2} = \frac{2(60)(40)}{60 + 40} = \frac{4800}{100} = 48\text{ km/h}$.

questions.q: Two trains leave the same station in opposite directions at speeds of $70\text{ km/h}$ and $80\text{ km/h}$. In how many hours will they be $450\text{ km}$ apart?
questions.answer: Relative speed in opposite directions $= 70 + 80 = 150\text{ km/h}$. Time $= \frac{\text{Distance}}{\text{Relative Speed}} = \frac{450}{150} = 3$ hours.

questions.q: A cyclist travels $15\text{ km}$ in $45$ minutes. What is their speed in kilometers per hour?
Pipe A can fill a tank in $6$ hours, while Pipe B can fill it in $3$ hours. If both pipes are opened together, how long will it take to fill the tank?
questions.answer: Combined rate $= \frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{3} = \frac{1}{6} + \frac{2}{6} = \frac{3}{6} = \frac{1}{2}$ tank/hour. Time required $= 2$ hours.
